answer.rationale: The strongest causal signal is temporal: a release shipped 2 hours ago and the write-path p99 began climbing 90 minutes ago, inside that window. Region-confinement is ambiguous evidence — it is consistent with a regionally-staged release rollout as much as with a regional infrastructure fault — so it does not by itself favor failover. Failover (memory_b2) is attractive because it worked in March, but it is the wrong tool if the defect travels with the build: we would carry the regression into the secondary region while draining and re-pointing a primary that is currently absorbing peak settlement writes, which is precisely the maneuver most likely to lose in-flight customer writes. add_capacity (memory_b3) treats a surge, and settlement peak is expected, not anomalous. route_read_replicas (memory_b5) relieves read pressure on the primary, but the symptom is write-path latency and settlement traffic is write-heavy, so the mechanism does not match. Circuit breakers (memory_b4) contained a partner dependency failure; no partner fault is indicated here, and failing fast on writes would shed exactly the writes we are told not to lose. I verify memory_b1 rather than the failover memory because b1 is the memory actually driving my action and its stated evidence is a checkout error spike, not a latency ramp — I need the original record to see whether the rollback resolved a latency regression or only an error-rate one, and whether "the prior build was stable" was confirmed or assumed. If b1 turns out to be error-spike-only, my confidence in rollback as a latency remedy drops and failover moves up. I scope this as a small guarded test because memory_b6 shows this org can gate by cohort: roll back a bounded slice of primary-region write traffic, confirm p99 recovers in that slice, and only then widen. That buys causal confirmation without a full-fleet build change during peak, and it is reversible if latency does not respond. Residual uncertainty I am not resolving: I have no direct confirmation the release touched the write path, and a coincident infrastructure fault remains live. All six inherited memories are single successful episodes with no recorded failures, so they tell me which interventions have worked, not how often they were tried — I am treating them as weaker evidence than their confident tone suggests.
